generalProvisions: This bill amends provisions relating to consumer protection.
highlightedProvisions: This bill:<hr><ltbullet>defines terms;<hr><ltbullet>renumbers Title 13, Chapter 2, Division of Consumer Protection;<hr><ltbullet>renumbers Title 13, Chapter 21, Credit Services Organizations Act;<hr><ltbullet>renumbers Title 13, Chapter 22, Charitable Solicitations Act;<hr><ltbullet>renumbers and renames Title 13, Chapter 23, Health Spa Services Protection Act;<hr><ltbullet>renumbers Title 13, Chapter 26, Telephone Fraud Prevention Act;<hr><ltbullet>adds Title 13, Chapter 77, Generative Artificial Intelligence - Consumer Disclosures and Enforcement, to the list of chapters the Division of Consumer Protection (division) enforces;<hr><ltbullet>amends the division's investigatory authority to investigate conduct related to statutes that the division administers and enforces;<hr><ltbullet>amends filing requirements a person makes with the division; <hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to an entity's surety bond and certificate of deposit;<hr><ltbullet>provides the circumstances under which the division may recover costs from a surety bond or a certificate of deposit;<hr><ltbullet>provides that a person correct information contained in a filing the person makes with the division if the information becomes incorrect or incomplete;<hr><ltbullet>provides that certain persons may not represent that the division or the state endorses or approves the person;<hr><ltbullet>clarifies that the issuance of certain documents does not constitute an approval or endorsement by the division or the state;<hr><ltbullet>provides the circumstances under which the division may deny, suspend, or revoke certain documents;<hr><ltbullet>requires that a person that registers with the division maintain a registered agent in this state;<hr><ltbullet>provides requirements for the information a person shall maintain for a registered agent in this state;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to the division's enforcement powers and penalties the division may impose;<hr><ltbullet>provides the actions a court may take when the division brings an enforcement action;<hr><ltbullet>provides the circumstances under which a court may order disgorgement of money;<hr><ltbullet>amends charitable solicitation financial report requirements;<hr><ltbullet>changes references in Title 13, Chapter 23, Health Spa Service Protection Act from "health spa" to "fitness center";<hr><ltbullet>provides registration and renewal requirements for certain entities and individuals;<hr><ltbullet>provides the length of a term for certain registrations;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to criminal background checks for an entity applying for registration with the division;<hr><ltbullet> provides that a seller or a seller's solicitor provide a consumer certain disclosures;<hr><ltbullet>provides the circumstances under which the attorney general shall give legal advice to and act as counsel for the division;<hr><ltbullet>updates terminology to refer to the division;<hr><ltbullet>removes redundant provisions from provisions the division enforces;<hr><ltbullet>amends provisions relating to an annual report a person is required to file with the division;<hr><ltbullet>removes references to the attorney general's enforcement powers in relation to the division; and<hr><ltbullet>makes technical and conforming changes.
